Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 4)
Topic: Shiv Tattva, Kul Devta & the Pitru Game — Why Marriages Fail or Survive

Source: Bhaiya's satsang session (video transcript, ~1hr 29min), part of the Mool Tattva series. Continues the previous Mool Tattva sessions on: why pitrs pass on their siddhis, the Kul Devta concept (three aspects), and the Shiv Tattva (what it is, the three ways it is lost, and how losing it costs a person their partner, charm, and standing). Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version.
1. SHIV TATTVA — HOW IT IS ACTUALLY OBTAINED (Recap + Deepening)
Mantra gives energy — NOT Shiv Tattva

From physical activities you can gain some Shiv Tattva: good sattvik food, good drink, sattvik living. But in its extensive/real form, only the devtas can grant Shiv Tattva. And devtas are pleased through mantra.

Critical distinction: "Mantra se banti hai SHAKTI (energy). Shiv Tattva alag hai." Any mantra you chant — of Bholenath, of Mata, of anyone — pr oduces urja/energy. It is a myth (veham) that chanting Bholenath's mantra gives Shiv Tattva while Mata's does not. Shiv Tattva is received only when a devta personally comes — gives darshan/sakshatkar — and grants it. Without darshan, without sakshatkar, without siddhi, no amount of jaap gives you Shiv Tattva. The jaap builds the energy; the devta's appearance converts it. What do you actually receive at darshan? Grahan Shakti (the capacity to receive) — "Grahan Shakti hi Shiv Tattva hai." The receiving-capacity itself IS the Shiv Tattva.
What saints/sants can and cannot give

Sants can NEVER give Shiv Tattva — only devtas give it. What sants give is support: a mala, a katora (bowl), jal/amrit — items that help you hold on for some time. The "astral opium" concept: just as opium is medically used to keep body functions steady (heart patients, infants' organ function, high altitudes, focus), in the sukshma jagat santmahatmas administer an equivalent — they chant a mantra, blow it into water, and give it to drink — pr oducing an astral nasha (intoxication) that boosts the sukshma sharir's focus and concentration during sadhna. It works astrally exactly as it works physically, and lasts for a limited period. This is the meaning behind Neem Karoli Baba's "Ram naam ka nasha karo" — Bhaiya says he has personally seen sants administering the "intoxication of Ram's name" this way. (Bhaiya calls him "Neem Karoli Bhagwan" — for he is Bhagwan, not mer ely a Maharaj.) Guru Tattva = Shiv Tattva in its highest abundance. "A lifetime's earnings and one moment of the Guru's company are equal — because the Guru car ries Shiv Tattva in boundless measure."
How to increase your Shiv Tattva (the practice)

1. Do jaap (builds the energy). 2. Do sadhna in the Guru's sanidhya (company/shelter) and take his ashirwad. 3. Wait — until dev shakti is attained, Shiv T attva will not come. When it starts coming, you will begin to see it around you. 4. Do not make yourself a hero until you have had darshan.
On siddhi claims

Forget those who say "I've chanted for three months, I have a siddhi." "The day you truly have a siddhi, you will not need to announce it — people will come and kiss your feet. A siddhi displays its own supremacy (varchasva)." When a real shakti comes to you, it shows its own miracle and leaves YOU stunned.

Case: a member of a big institute had his aura checked; mentor Shivotsav Bhaiya (very straightforward) told him plainly — "you have a negativity that eats your body's jaap and considers itself a hero; you are lying about having a siddhi. If you had a siddhi, WE would be kissing YOUR feet." Whoever holds real siddhi holds Shiv Tattva in abundance — and his partner sits ﬁr mly at his left side (vaam bhaag); he never needs to chase anyone.
2. WHY MARRIAGES DON'T HAPPEN OR DON'T SURVIVE — THE TWO CAUSES
Bhaiya's diagnostic framework for "shaadi nahi ho rahi / rishtey nahi tikte":
Cause 1 — Devta (Kul Devta) dosh → aﬀects the WHOLE family

When devta-dosh is present, marriages fail across the entire family: the ﬁrst son's marriage doesn't happen; the second's happens with great struggle then ends in divorce; the daughter's doesn't happen, or happens and breaks — twice. L ook at the whole family and you will ﬁnd everyone disturbed. That patter n = devta's cause. When devtas are displeased, even marriages that happen keep breaking — they don't hold.
Cause 2 — Personal Shiv Tattva deﬁciency → aﬀects the individual

Without Shiv Tattva you lose holding capacity / attraction power — you cannot hold a partner; they drift away. Everyone's Shiv Tattva diﬀers fr om childhood. Strong Shiv Tattva → marriage happens, partner sits in your vaam bhaag, no one can take them. Moderate Shiv Tattva → every time an outside negativity attacks, you'll have to plead your partner back again and again. And if a tantrik kriya lands on you at that vulnerable time, your remaining Shiv Tattva is pulled out (as taught in the previous session) — "your R am naam satya hai" — you ar e left alone.
How the two interact

Devta's kripa + no Shiv Tattva → partner strays, ﬁghts happen, bitter ness — but you will never separate, because the devta holds a boundary the partner cannot cross. ("Look at your own parents: rolling pins ﬂying, utensils ﬂying — yet food is cook ed under one roof. That distant bonding is the devta's doing.") Shiv Tattva present + devta displeased → a partner keeps arriving (Shiv Tattva pushes again and again) but the marriage keeps breaking (devta's conﬂict). Both present → everything runs beautifully. Bhaiya: even today, more than 75% of households are intact and clean — Gujarat, R ajasthan, MP, even Delhi — wher ever dev shaktis still run in
the kul, marriages and children ﬂourish. Even untimely deaths trace back to the Shiv T attva– devta pair.
3. KUL DEVTA — THE COMPLETE CONCEPT
Their jurisdiction (three main works)

The Kul Devta's three principal responsibilities: 1. Vansh — who will tak e birth in your family (boy/girl, santaan prapti). 2. Marriage — whom you will mar ry. 3. Lineage protection — holding the family's line (lineage) together within their boundary.
Regional Kul Devtas — Bhomiya Ji, Goga Ji & the crossroads Mata

Bhomiya Ji is a genuine devta (kul devta category, "gramin" — village deity), heavily r evered in Haryana and Rajasthan. "Bhomiya Ji se panga nahi lena" — if you fail to worship him, he will let you know. Goga Ji (Goga Peer) runs parallel — "Jathe khejdi, bathe Gogo" (wher e the khejri tree is, there is Goga) is the Rajasthani saying. Where Goga Peer is, Bhomiya Ji is too. (Ramdev Ji also mentioned in this family of deities.) These run parallel to the Matas (Chauganan Mata and the Matas who accompany Sheetla Mata). In some families the kul devta seat is held by a Mata; in others by these devtas. Chauganan Mata is the crossroads devi, found at every chauraha — a classic sign of her displeasure: vehicles stalling at crossroads (car/bike/scooty dying exactly at the chauraha and restarting after). Bhomiya Ji and Goga Peer are likewise found at crossroads.
The relationship rules: Prem vs Family (the Anshu analogy)

Isht/Guru = a PREM (love) relationship. Like Bhaiya and Anshu's brother-sister bond: even if one does nothing for the other, the other still does. Your Isht — e.g., Hanuman Ji Maharaj — is lik e this: miss a day, and Baba stands in for you: "he's my boy; he missed it, I'll mark his attendance." Kul Devta = a FAMILY (reciprocity) relationship. Between two families, if one doesn't honor the other, the other stops honoring back. "Until you do for the Kul Devta, they will not do for you." That is the family reet — and the e xact Kul Devta principle. Boundaries and adhikaar (authority): love does not equal authority. However much prem Anshu has, she cannot cross a certain boundary — not for lack of love, but lack of adhik aar. Likewise your Isht cannot do the works that fall inside the family's personal domain — those belong to the Kul Devta's jurisdiction. Hanuman Ji Maharaj will perform kul devta duties ONLY in the family where he IS the kul devta. This is exactly why the devta (kul devta) became necessary — no one else is authorized to do their work.
Why devta shaktis have weakened in this generation

Earlier, daughters-in-law simply did what the elders said — "k eep this vrat, bow to Bhomiya Ji, bow to Goga Ji, this prasad here, this pheri there" — continuously, without questions. That obedience kept the devtas' shaktis bound to the family. Today: "if-but-why-question-mark" culture, liberalism, equality — "Equality is ﬁne — k eep it between yourselves. Don't drag the devtas into it." The new generation stopped going ("why go to THAT mandir — God is everywher e, we'll worship right here"). The devtas have been pushed to the back foot, so they stopped doing their work. And when devtas step back, all you're left with is your own Shiv Tattva. Meanwhile, pitrs have built a monopoly: generation after generation they have occupied the Kul Devta's sthaan, so even the bhog oﬀer ed no longer reaches the devta.
What the Kul Devta actually wants (the simple contract)

The Kul Devta does NOT want puja-paath, sadhna, or bhakti from you — generations of your family have already done that; the shakti is already established in your home. The Kul Devta asks only for BHOG: nariyal, tel, deepak, pheri at their sthaan, prasad — the traditional oﬀerings. "Jitna bhog doge, utna milega." In Aashray, this is honored through Kul Devta havans and deepaks (every Friday for the past year, Aashray runs Kul Devta sessions where each member's kul devta is identiﬁed and the tarang explained). When you perform a Kul Devta havan, the tarang begins arriving within 2 months 22 days. Those who showed samarpan to their kul devta this past year have seen drastic life changes. BUT: bhog alone will not get you personal Shiv Tattva. The Kul Devta will do everything inside their jurisdiction (hold your partner inside the boundary, protect the line) in exchange for bhog — but to r eceive personal Shiv Tattva from them, you must adopt them as Isht (or Guru) and do their SADHNA — then they manifest (prak at) and grant it.
Havan mechanics (proportions & waves)

Beneﬁts ar e proportional, never equal: the person who commissions/sits in the havan with sankalp receives the most; the rest of the family receives less but still receives. Same for the one family member who does the daily deepak taking everyone's names — the aavahan-k arta always receives the most, since the tarang ﬂows to others through him/her. Tarang never ﬂows constantly — it ar rives in waves, like a heartbeat.
4. PITRU DOSH vs PITRU SAMASYA (Important distinction)
Pitru DOSH = lies on the WHOLE family (everyone carries a bit of it, never equally).

Pitru SAMASYA = individual — a pitru actually seated in ONE particular person's body; that person bears the brunt (others may even call them "mad"). One sibling can carry a severe pitru samasya while another has none. Pitrs disproportionately occupy women's bodies in a family. This unevenness is why, in one house, four members stay utterly stuck ("nikamme") while two ﬂourish — the dosh was on all, but the grip was on those four . (Contrast with Kul Devta havan beneﬁts, which spr ead across the family — pitru pr oblems concentrate in individuals.)
5. THE PITRU GAME — HOW WEDDINGS ARE SABOTAGED (the love-marriage case study)
Why some marriages are never "accepted" — nar rated as a full case study (the "Ritesh" scenario, with a real member conﬁr ming it happened to her):

1. Setup: A boy ﬁx es a love marriage (diﬀer ent caste; parents obsessed with pleasing children agree — helped along by dowry temptations, the "F ortuner" satire). The household pitrs — whom the family itself invited back during the 12/13-day death rituals — watch everything. 2. The pitrs' countermove: knowing they'll be sidelined, the pitru-mukhiya ﬁrst claims all the household bhog/sweets and distributes it to all the pitrs and negativities of the whole area — an open invitation feast. Once fed through him, they all come under his command. (By default, ﬁrst authority over a house's food belongs to the pitrs.) 3. On the wedding day, they make sure no dev shakti is present. Three ways the wedding sankalp fails: the pandit is not jagrit / takes no proper sankalp; OR no dev shakti is present at the venue; OR the pitrs mount someone's head and rush the ceremony ("take 2000, take 5000, ﬁnish it fast"). A confused (bhramit) human cannot perfor m a true aavahan — and pitrs specialize in confusing. 4. Result: the devtas never arrive → the Kul Devta never ACCEPTS the marriage → the pitrs occupy the kul devta's seat for the event. 5. The bride's fate: since the Kul Devta never accepted her, in the astral ledger she is not the family's daughter — she is an OUTSIDER . "Do anything to her inside the house — no one will say anything, because she does not belong to the kul. Where would she even ﬁle her complaint?" The pitrs then get unrestricted rights over her. - "Man is an animal that behaves well only under restriction. Remove restriction, and there is no more dangerous animal — the same applies to pitrs given fr ee rein." 6. Symptoms in real life: the girl falls ill immediately after moving into the new house ("I was never sick before I came here"); constant escalating ﬁghts; she loses her var chasva, then her mastishk (mental clarity); pitrs begin to sit in her body; the husband's life also collapses; and whatever dowry came (the Fortuner) is destroyed by your own hands — "k eep ﬁlling its tank;

it will keep emptying." - Real testimony in-session: a member conﬁr med — medicines stopped working, cholesterol 200→400 in a month, depression/anxiety, dissociation ("the house was on ﬁr e in front of me and my mind would not react"). "If I had not left, I would have been ﬁnished." Bhaiya: "Y es — your namo -nishan would not have remained." 7. Slow torture is the preferred method: actual maran kriya is rare (5 in 100, death in 15–20 days). The daily kriya is tadpana — push the person to the brink, pull back, r epeat for a lifetime: "killing is once; tormenting is the greater sport." You can neither stay nor leave. 8. When is this scenario most likely? When the boy's and girl's KUL DEVTAS ARE NOT THE SAME (and the wedding aavahan failed). Same/compatible kul devta = "balle-balle." (Note: many communities deliberately marry OUTSIDE their own kul devta — that is their tradition and works within its own rules; and if a community has generations of successful love marriages, their pitrs are favorable. Not every love marriage is doomed — this is the failure mechanism, not a verdict on love marriage itself. 80% of some communities' marriages are love marriages and succeed.) 9. Resolution exists — Aashray has a pr ocess for getting the bride accepted by the Kul Devta (special protocols, done in guru-sanidhya; kul devta havans / pitru-negativity havans). It has been done many times. Mool Tattva sessions are analysis-only; for the resolution, contact your mentor.
Willpower footnote

"When a human resolves to do something, no power in the universe can stop him — even Bhagwan steps aside for that one moment: 'ﬁne, do it.'" Those who claim "negativity ruined my exam" — no, your own mind wasn't in it. The same ir on will that forces a marriage through is the will that could have done the jaap. Pitrs can only delay and distort; the mann is yours.
6. THE PITRU REBIRTH REPLICA — "CHACHA JI IS BACK"
The second great pitru game, explained at length:

1. Families proudly say: "our departed always take rebirth in our own family — they even announce it: 'I will return.'" 2. What actually happens: when a child is about to be born, a recently-departed pitru declares "this body is mine." All other pitrs step aside. From birth onward, that pitru enters the child gradually through food (by default all household food passes through the pitrs' sanidhya — he rides the food's tattvas in, again and again). By age ~10, the pitru is fully seated in the child's body. 3. Because the pitru occupied the body early, the child's own sukshma sharir is never allowed to form.

4. The pitru can recall old memories and claim identity. Any aura-checker/pandit/drishti-wala then says "isn't this your chacha?" — and the family falls at the child's feet: "Chacha aa gaye! Chacha, bless us, protect the house!" The pitru plays along: "I will handle everything, tension mat lo… tathastu." 5. Every blessing, tattva, and devta-tarang meant for the child now goes equally — or ﬁrst — to the seated pitru ("the body is his," says the pitru). The child grows up carrying not only his own ﬂaws but the pitru's full k aam-krodh-lobh-moh-matsar. He can never settle on one tattva — the child lik es one thing, the chacha likes another. ("He's exactly like chacha ji!" — "Check pr operly — it might BE chacha ji.") 6. At death, the pitru shows himself — "it was me all along" — and moves to the ne xt body: "follow me; do exactly as I do."
Where the pitrs learned this trick

In earlier times, families would go to sant-mahatmas and pray: "may we have a lalla like YOU; may your tattva, your kripa, your tarang come to our child" — R am tattva, Shiv tattva, Bhole ka tattva. The pitrs WATCHED this happen repeatedly — and humans (and sukshma sharirs) ar e copy masters: "we only know how to copy; I too am copying what Baba tells me." The pitrs replicate the ritual — but the replica has none of the sant's tattva: "the chacha who came back has nothing of a real chacha in him." The original miracle carried a mahapurush's tattva; the copy carries a pitru's vices. That is why we are suﬀering so much — the same cer emony, hollowed out. No one updates "the astral world's homepage": the physical world changed, the sukshma jagat keeps changing with us, but families keep running the old protocols blindly.
The shraddh paradox

Who invited the pitrs home in the ﬁrst place? You did — the 12/13-day rituals: oﬀering Ganga snan there, then coming home and doing aavahan-bhog in the departed's name (feeding cows, placing food on the roof). "You called him the very same day — of course he came. And having been called, he stays — in your own body — for life. Then you complain 'pitrs don't leave.'" Western countries don't perform these rites — cor respondingly few pitru cases (2–3 in 10, handled when needed). BUT — and this is crucial — you cannot abandon the riti-riwaz , or your own family/society will cast you out (consistent with Session 3's rule: never break tradition). The answer is not rebellion but knowledge + shakti: know what the ritual does, and use dev shaktis (guru-sanidhya, havans) to keep pitrs in their place.
7. AASHRAY'S STANCE & CLOSING NOTES

"Aashray is an institute which studies and does deep analysis into the astral world and its working. We tell you the real-life facts — doing or not doing is up to you." Bhaiya states he has never described anything he has not personally seen. "Facts are fair. Life is fair — neither good nor bad." Mool T attva videos feel harsh because they carry the truth; whoever wants truth must accept it — and whoever wants to verif y it should open their own drishti and look. Bhaiya's challenge: Mool Tattva teachings match no granth anywhere — yet if any of it is ever proven wrong, "we will leave our gaddi." It is Gurudev's vani, and it has never been wrong. Standing reminder: everyone's Gurudev is Hanuman Ji Maharaj; Bhaiya teaches as that Guru's disciple from the guru-gaddi. "Learn if you wish; don't if you don't — the Guru has discharged his duty." Closing invitations: Mahayagya (next day) — come with your sank alp, awaken bhakti, receive Gurudev's kripa; then attend Deep Prajwalan.
8. QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. Mantra jaap builds energy; only a devta's darshan converts it into Shiv Tattva (= grahan shakti). No darshan, no Shiv Tattva. 2. Sants support (mala, katora, abhimantrit jal — astral "nasha" for focus); they cannot grant Shiv Tattva. The Guru carries it boundlessly. 3. Real siddhi announces itself — never announce yours; don't play her o before darshan. 4. Marriage problems have exactly two roots: Kul Devta dosh (whole family pattern) and personal Shiv Tattva deﬁciency (no holding/attraction power). Check the family patter n ﬁrst. 5. Kul Devta = family reciprocity: give bhog (nariyal, tel, deepak, pheri, havan) and they work; ignore them and they stop. Their shakti is already established — they don't need your sadhna, only your bhog. 6. For personal Shiv Tattva from the Kul Devta, go further: adopt them as Isht and do sadhna until they manifest. 7. Kul Devta havan → tarang within 2 months 22 days; the sankalp-taker receives most; tarang ﬂows in waves. 8. Pitru dosh is family-wide; pitru samasya is individual (often in women). Never assume equal distribution. 9. Weddings fail astrally when the aavahan fails (weak pandit / no dev shakti / pitru interference) — then the K ul Devta never accepts the bride, leaving her an unprotected "outsider." Resolution exists via mentor + guru-sanidhya protocols.

10. Beware the rebirth replica: a pitru claiming "I returned" blocks the child's own sukshma sharir and eats the child's blessings. Verify with real drishti before celebrating "chacha's return." 11. Keep performing your riti-riwaz (never break tradition/society) — but with knowledge, and with dev shakti guarding the door. 12. Willpower footnote: what your mann truly resolves, nothing can stop — pitrs e xploit confusion, not strength.
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 4, English)
Shiv Tattva, Kul Devta & the Pitru Game
User-style questions with answers grounded in Bhaiya's discourse. Greeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. If I chant Bholenath's mantra, will I get Shiv Tattva? A: Jai Siya Ram! This is a common myth. ANY mantra — Bholenath's, Mata's, anyone's — pr oduces energy (urja/shakti), not Shiv Tattva. "Mantra se banti hai shakti; Shiv Tattva alag hai." Shiv Tattva is received only when a devta personally gives darshan/sakshatkar and grants it. Your jaap builds the energy; the devta's appearance converts it. What you receive at darshan is grahan shakti — the capacity to r eceive — and grahan shakti itself IS Shiv T attva.

Q2. So how do I actually increase my Shiv Tattva? A: Four steps: (1) keep doing jaap — that builds the energy; (2) do sadhna in the Guru's sanidhya and take his ashirwad; (3) physically support it with sattvik food, drink, and living; (4) wait — until dev shakti is attained, Shiv T attva will not come, and when it starts coming you will see it around you. And one rule: don't make yourself a hero until you have had darshan.

Q3. Can a sant or any person give me Shiv Tattva? A: No human can. If a human could increase Shiv Tattva, that human would be Bhagwan. Sants give SUPPORT — a mala, a k atora, abhimantrit jal/amrit (mantra blown into water) that produces an astral "nasha" boosting your sukshma sharir's focus for a time — lik e opium steadies the body medically. This is the meaning of Neem Karoli Baba's "Ram naam ka nasha karo." But the tattva itself only devtas grant. The Guru, however, carries Shiv Tattva boundlessly — one moment of the Guru's company equals a lifetime's earnings.

Q4. I've done jaap for months — I think I have a siddhi. How do I conﬁrm? A: The day you truly have a siddhi, you will not need to conﬁr m or announce it — people will come and kiss your feet. A siddhi displays its own supremacy; a real shakti shows its own miracle and leaves YOU stunned. Those who go around getting auras checked to prove their siddhi usually carry a negativity that eats their jaap and fancies itself a hero. Stay humble, keep the jaap.
Q5. Marriages in my whole family keep failing or breaking. Why? A: When the pattern covers the WHOLE family — one sibling's mar riage doesn't happen, another's happens with

struggle then divorces, a third's breaks twice — that is K ul Devta dosh. When devtas are displeased, even completed marriages don't hold. Solution path: restore the Kul Devta relationship — bhog, deepak, pheri, and K ul Devta havans (tarang begins within 2 months 22 days). Talk to your mentor for your family's speciﬁc case.

Q6. My marriage isn't happening / partners keep leaving ME speciﬁcally . Why? A: That points to the second cause — personal Shiv T attva deﬁciency . Without Shiv Tattva you lose holding capacity and attraction power; you cannot hold a partner. If your Shiv Tattva is moderate, every outside negativity attack forces you to win your partner back again and again — and if a tantrik kriya lands in that window, the remaining Shiv Tattva is pulled out. Build it back: jaap + guru-sanidhya sadhna + devta's kripa.

Q7. My parents ﬁght constantly but never separate. What holds them? A: The devta's boundary. When the Kul Devta is with a couple, the partner may stray emotionally, ﬁghts may ﬂy ("chakla-belan udte hain"), but neither can cross the devta's line — food still cooks under one roof. That distant bonding is the devta's doing. The new generation lacks this because they stopped honoring the devtas.

Q8. Who are Bhomiya Ji and Goga Ji? A: Genuine devtas of the Kul Devta category, greatly revered in Haryana and Rajasthan. "Jathe khejdi, bathe Gogo" — wher e Goga Peer is, Bhomiya Ji is too. They run parallel to the Matas (Chauganan Mata, the companions of Sheetla Mata) — in some families the kul devta seat is a Mata, in others these devtas. Do not take Bhomiya Ji lightly — neglect his worship and he will mak e it known. Classic sign of the crossroads devi's displeasure: vehicles stalling exactly at chaurahas.

Q9. What does the Kul Devta actually want from me? Do I need to do their sadhna? A: Beautifully simple: the Kul Devta does NOT want puja-paath, sadhna, or bhakti — generations of your family already did that, and the shakti is already established in your home. The Kul Devta asks only for BHOG: nariyal, tel, deepak, pheri at their sthaan, havan. Give bhog and they work; the more you give, the more you receive. It is a family-reciprocity relationship: until you do for them, they will not do for you.

Q10. Then what's the diﬀerence between my K ul Devta and my Isht? A: The relationship type. Isht/Guru is a PREM relationship — lik e a loving sibling: miss a day of your practice and Hanuman Ji Maharaj still stands in for you ("he's my boy — I'll mark his attendance"). K ul Devta is a FAMILY relationship — strict r eciprocity. And remember jurisdiction: love does not equal authority. Your Isht cannot perform works that fall in the Kul Devta's domain (vansh, marriage, lineage) — unless he IS your k ul devta. Each shakti works within its boundary.

Q11. If I do a Kul Devta havan, does the beneﬁt reach my whole family? A: Yes, but proportionally — never equally . The one who commissions it and sits with sankalp receives the most; the tarang ﬂows to the r est through that person, so others receive less but still receive. Same with a daily deepak done in everyone's names — the aavahan-k arta always receives most. And note: tarang never ﬂows constantly; it ar rives in waves, like a heartbeat.

Q12. What's the diﬀerence between pitru dosh and pitru samasya? A: Pitru DOSH lies on the whole family — everyone car ries some, never equally. Pitru SAMASYA is individual — an actual pitru seated in one particular person's body, who bears the brunt (and is often called mad by the rest). Pitrs disproportionately occupy women's bodies. This is why four members of a house can stay stuck while two ﬂourish.

Q13. Why did my health and mind collapse right after I moved into my in-laws' home? A: This matches the "unaccepted bride" pattern. If the wedding's aavahan failed — a pandit who took no real sankalp, no dev shakti present, or pitru interference rushing the ceremony — then the Kul Devta never accepted you, and astrally you are an "outsider" in that house, unprotected, with the household pitrs holding unrestricted rights. Q15. Why don't pitrs just kill the person they torment? A: Bhaiya's chilling observation: actual maran kriya is rare — at most 5 in 100 cases, death in 15–20 days. Q16. Our family believes our departed elders take rebirth among us. Is that real? A: Listen carefully — this is one of the pitru world's biggest games. When a child is due, a departed pitru claims "this body is mine," enters the child gradually through household food (all food passes through the pitrs' sanidhya by default), and is fully seated by about age 10 — pr eventing the child's OWN sukshma sharir from forming. The family celebrates, and every blessing meant for the child is intercepted by the seated pitru — the child gr ows up carrying the pitru's kaam-krodh-lobh-moh too. Q17. Where did pitrs learn this rebirth trick? A: From us. Earlier, families went to santmahatmas praying "may our lalla be like YOU — your tattva, your tarang, your kripa." The pitrs watched this repeated for generations — and sukshma sharirs, lik e humans, are copy masters. They replicate the ceremony, but the replica carries no sant's tattva — only the pitru's vices. Q18. Did we ourselves invite our pitrs home? A: Yes — the shraddh parado x. The answer is knowledge plus shakti: perform the rites knowing what they do, and keep dev shaktis (gurusanidhya, havans) guarding the door.

Q19. Can negativity make me fail my exam or stop my work? A: Bhaiya's counter: when a human truly resolves, no power in the universe can stop him — even Bhagwan steps aside for that moment. "Negativity ruined my exam" usually means your own mann wasn't in it. Pitrs and negativity exploit confusion (bhram) — they cannot beat a made-up mind. The same will that forces through a love marriage against all odds could master the jaap.
